dedupe_keys.name: stochastic occupant behaviour simulator for the resstock u s housing stock model

description: A stochastic simulator of the energy-related behaviour of individual household members, combined with the ResStock housing stock model to give more realistic residential load profiles, described in a November 2021 arXiv paper by a team including Jianli Chen and Eric Wilson. Most building energy models use fixed, homogeneous occupant schedules, which suit annual totals but give exaggerated or muted hourly peaks, and this matters as variable renewables, batteries and grid-interactive buildings spread. The authors first cluster American Time Use Survey activity patterns, then simulate behaviour with time-inhomogeneous Markov chains and probabilistic sampling of event durations. The output feeds EnergyPlus power and hot water schedules through ResStock, so loads can be simulated for communities, cities, states and the nation. Results were checked against American Time Use Survey data and measured end-use electricity data. Coverage: the United States housing stock. Access: the paper only; no code link was found on the pages read; the paper is CC BY 4.0. Useful for demand planning and grid interaction studies; it builds on the ResStock record in the catalogue.
